data.author: jbeirer

- **Constraint units:** evaluators declare the unit of each metric; a constraint with a different unit is rejected before the geometry is materialized or ddsim starts.

- **Provenance:** absolute, URL and `$` file references on non-include elements are listed as external in the manifest (still outside the fingerprint).
- **Docs:** problem and geometry docs match the implemented behavior.

Regression tests added for each; unit suite, mypy and pre-commit pass.

data.title: geometry: cap include depth, stop on looping directory symlinks
data.author: jbeirer
data.body:
Deep include chains (500 files) leaked RecursionError; they now raise IncludeError beyond 100 nested levels.

A directory symlink looping back (`loop -> .`) made the walker revisit the same physical file under ever longer lexical directories until the OS symlink limit; such re-entry is now skipped like any include cycle.

Both cases have regression tests.

data.title: geometry: alias-aware overrides and symlink validation
data.author: jbeirer
data.body:
Fixes two alias-related materialization issues, on top of the include-alias fixes already on this branch.

- Changed `ref` attributes are resolved from every name (symlink) of the edited file, so resources and includes needed by each alias directory are copied and recorded in the manifest.
- Discovered symlink aliases are verified against the source before copying; a retargeted link raises `MaterializationError` and asks for rediscovery.

Regression tests added for all three cases.

data.title: geometry: fingerprint aliases, aliased include traversal, manifest and YAML robustness
data.author: jbeirer
data.body:
## Changes

- **Fingerprint:** include the effective file-alias mapping (catalog plus override-introduced), so geometries differing only in a symlink target no longer collide.
- **Include traversal:** a symlinked include in another directory is scanned again from its own directory, so its relative includes are discovered, copied and editable.
- **Manifest:** external references are listed once.
- **Config:** deeply nested YAML raises `ConfigError` instead of `RecursionError`.

Each fix has a regression test. The aliased-include fix assumes DD4hep resolves relative includes against the path as written, not the symlink target; the DD4hep integration tests were not run here.

data.title: geometry: keep symlinked include names, follow redirected includes, fall back on EOPNOTSUPP
data.author: jbeirer
data.body:
Fixes three geometry materialization edge cases and clarifies the fingerprint scope.

- A file included under several symlinked names is copied once; the other names become relative links in the snapshot, so edits reach every name and the snapshot stays self-consistent.
- An override that redirects an include `ref` now brings the new XML file, its transitive includes, resources and outside-root references into the snapshot and the fingerprint. A redirect to a missing file fails early with a clear error.
- `_publish()` falls back to a plain rename on `EOPNOTSUPP`, as it already does for `ENOSYS` and `EINVAL`.
- Docs: the fingerprint identifies the locally captured inputs only; an evaluation cache key must also include the software stack and external dependencies.

Tests added for each case;…

data.author: jbeirer
data.body:

data.title: Fix CI: make the source-root test independent of git, skip hooks in CI
data.author: jbeirer
data.body:
The first CI run failed in the `test` job with one failing unit test.

- `test_environment_variables_are_expanded` assumed the checkout is recognized as a git repository. In the CI container the workspace is owned by another user, so git refuses it and root detection correctly falls back to the file's directory. The expected compact path is now derived from the detected root.
- `setup.sh` no longer installs the git hooks when `CI` is set: nobody commits there, and downloading the hook environments is wasted time.

Checked locally: lint, strict mypy and the unit tests pass; in a clean copy with `CI=true` the 127 unit tests pass and the hook step is skipped.

data.title: [IDEA] Read the GGTF model from --trackingModel, download only if missing
data.author: jbeirer
data.body:
Closes #406.

`IDEA_o1_v03/run_digi_reco.py` downloaded the GGTF model with `wget -O` every time the options file was read, so every `k4run` needed network access and fetched ~65 MB again, even when the model was already there. That download also lands inside the time k4Bench measures for the IDEA reconstruction benchmarks.

This PR:

- adds `--trackingModel` for the path to the model. The default is still `SimpleGatrIDEAv3o1.onnx` in the run directory, so nothing changes for existing workflows.
- downloads the model only if that file doesn't exist. The download goes to a temporary file that is renamed once it is complete, so a failed download doesn't leave a broken model behind for the next run.
- takes the model from `fccsw.web.cern.ch`, the same file the README and `ctest_sim_digi_reco.…
